newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on declining turnover on Thursday in what traders termed another day of profit-taking.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 0.83 percent, or 2.12 points, to 252.69 on all-share turnover of 123 million shekels against 129 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.30 percent lower at 259.01.
"The session opened with mild gains following the Dow's rise on Wednesday, but by midday the trend changed and prices started falling," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.

"We were all waiting for a consolidation and it's very good that it finally came. The fact that volume is also declining indicates that this is only a correction and not the beginning of a negative trend," Nahum said.

"A correction is natural after such a strong rise and it is not surprising at all. The market was reacting to expectations that the central bank would not reduce its key lending rate following the release of January consumer price index (CPI)," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.

Nahum added that it is difficult to predict how the CPI, due to be published on Friday, will affect trading next week. "The main question is what have housing prices done," he said. "The market expects a CPI figure of around 0.5 percent and it's difficult to say if this will lead to another rate cut."
Traders noted that for the second day the market's decline was led by the blue chips while the small-capitalisation stocks traded on the karam continued rising.
"The rise of the karam stocks indicates that investors are still very optimistic," Kolka said.

The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 3.5 percent to 1,851 agorot on volume of 7.4 million shekels. Teva's American depositary receipts, which are traded on Nasdaq, rose 3.3 percent on Wednesday.

Other active shares included Discount Investment Corp, which lost 1.75 percent to 24,977 agorot on turnover of 4.0 million shekels, and Bank Hapoalim, which fell 2.75 percent to 643 agorot on volume of 4.0 million shekels.
